records.proposed_text: Memory claims must also specify access to time. The full-support opposing-target example rules out autonomous stationary finite-state controllers, yet a four-state controller with a free unbounded absolute clock achieves the separately proved finite lifetime error bound. The clock changes the controller model and can carry unbounded scheduling information; this result supplies neither an autonomous four-state realization nor a bound on restoration time or clock-computation cost.
records.qualification: Ordinary clocked construction and exact interval certificate, not a newly kernel-proved universal finite-memory theorem. Decision workspace and controller memory remain different.

records.proposed_text: The decision-complexity results concern different presentations. For the finite hidden-model support-menu criterion, compact support-independent or explicit Boolean-circuit menus give PSPACE-completeness, while a mandatory expanded table of every support menu gives polynomial time in that expanded input. Separately, the explicit posterior-deterministic model with mixed initial belief has a later ordinary EXPTIME-hardness reduction matching its EXPTIME upper bound; the earlier PSPACE-hard/in-EXPTIME gap is historical. These classifications are not controller-memory bounds, kernel-certified complexity proofs or the same input model.
records.qualification: Known initial state and actual initial observation/label assumptions are retained by the governing posterior-deterministic reduction. No collapsing of support-menu PSPACE theorem into PD EXPTIME theorem.
